scope: Implemented reference-contract differences; design choices accepted in decisions.json. Not upstream certification.

entries.reason: OpenAPI required must be an array; preserves the declared field.
Move required:true from path parameter schema to parameter. No request field added.
RefreshTokenResponse and WalletGrantRefreshTokenResponse overlap structurally, so validate token responses by the request grant type. Do not alter upstream oneOf.
Optional; accept the published account examples. STRICT_ACCOUNT_NAME is an explicit opt-in interoperability profile.
Use declared CONFIRMED/PENDING/REJECTED, not contradictory SUCCEEDED/FAILED examples.

Return200 REJECTED for cancelled/expired authorizations by default, with no confirmed_at. ENABLE_CANCELLED_LOOKUP=true opts into the explicit CANCELLED derived-runtime extension. Internal state remains CANCELLED.
Initial payout rejection uses the applicable declared400/422 detail; asynchronous rejection uses payoutCallback.

Allow one positive capture up to the authorization. Successful partial capture closes it and releases all unused hold; preserve authorized_e5 and store amount_e5 as actually captured. Refunds are capped at captured funds; another capture conflicts409.

Explicit funding-profile callback routing: new integrations use chargeCallback. Only legacy, opt-in deposit profiles use the upstream-deprecated confirmDeposit/cancelDeposit/updateDeposit. A reduced amount update precedes confirmation.
Unexpected/transient errors return retryable500 on every route, empty when undeclared, and are never cached. Authentication uses declared401, otherwise the existing declared400 mapping.
Reusable refresh tokens, 30-day configurable lifetime, 10-minute access tokens; code reuse revokes its issued family. No rotation field in refresh responses.

Return422 with BANK_HARD_ERROR/BANK_SOFT_ERROR. A definitive rejected capture does not debit and releases the entire original authorization, including a partial-capture attempt. Unknown transport outcomes remain retryable500/reconciliation.
An empty200 on successful cancellation.
Use Uber transaction/refund ID; merchant_reference, if supplied, must match.
Always include an immutable PSP reference, including rejection.
Code exchange returns refresh token; obtain access token using the refresh grant.
Use account_id and funding_method, with scoped account-bound bearer plus signature.

Use synchronous201 CONFIRMED then one REJECTED updateRefund by default. ENABLE_ASYNC_REFUND_REVERSAL=false refuses the synthetic two-callback funding profile; true is an explicit reference/test interpretation of the reversal exception. Never suppress an actual financial inverse. This is a delegated reference-owner decision, not an answer received from Uber.
Changed payload under the same payout ID or key returns409 DUPLICATE_REQUEST_ERROR; identical payload replays.

Closed UTC periods, daily by default; immutable confirmation/reversal journal; one canonical JSONL file per source account and a checksummed manifest; decimal-string signed E5 and per-currency totals. Seal once, reject overlaps, replay bytes. Atomic directory or strict-host-key local SFTP publication occurs outside SQL; transport receipt is not financial acceptance.

Relax only TransactionDescription.pattern by default; retain x-upstream-pattern for explicit strict opt-in, type and maxLength256. Published authentication example includes punctuation forbidden by its pattern.
Validate deprecated Account.uri, AccountOwner.uri and Deposit.uri as strings, not absolute URIs. The published example uses a network-path reference. Do not relax real action or redirect URL policy.

The literal authentication curl body also omits schema-required id and authorization, beyond the three R6 causes. Preserve it as a fixture and reject it unchanged; golden interoperability case supplies these two required fields and substitutes only the assigned funding method. Never derive a money identity or authorization from an informational field.

Use synchronous201 CONFIRMED then one REJECTED updateRefund by default. ENABLE_ASYNC_REFUND_REVERSAL=false refuses the synthetic two-callback funding profile; true is an explicit reference/test interpretation of the reversal exception. Never suppress an actual financial inverse. This is a delegated reference-owner decision, not an answer received from Uber.

Retain exact OAuth redirect_uri registration despite upstream discouraging allowlisting. Uber redirect changes must be registered first. Payment return_url has a separate scheme/authority/path allowlist preserving query bytes.
Authorize uses unsupported_response_type (RFC6749) rather than the inconsistent upstream unsupported_grant_type example; echo state only if supplied.

confirmDeposit/cancelDeposit/updateDeposit, charge.session_id, charge response merchant_reference/metadata, updateDeposit.metadata and all Account/AccountOwner/Deposit uri fields are upstream-deprecated. Legacy callbacks remain opt-in, not recommended for new integrations.
Keep find-transaction limited to charges/refunds and return404 for payout IDs. Payout recovery uses original provider-key reconciliation and callbacks; do not add an undeclared public operation.
Unsigned consent is rate-limited before persistence with429 and Retry-After60; validated internal errors use registered OAuth server_error redirects. No signed money-operation status is changed.

Bind every fresh client namespace to native runtime, storage version2 and independent instrument-key hash. Reject legacy/unversioned populated state, cross-language reuse or silent fingerprint-key changes. Rotating OAuth client credentials does not rotate instrument identity.

qualification: Reference design accepted by delegated project authority; no real-money mode or external certification is claimed.
